identification.title: All Heaven Declares
identification.notes: Words and music by Noel and Tricia Richards; a hymnal database records the copyright as 1987 Thankyou Music (Kingsway). The list's guess of Noel Richards is right but incomplete: Tricia Richards is a co-author. It is one of the couple's best-known songs and is in several hymnals and the Spring Harvest Praise! collection. No source read gives the story of its writing or its first recording, so album is left blank. The same database lists the key as Bb. Reviewed as the song, not any one recording.

claims.structuralNotes: A short song of one verse and one chorus, with the chorus carrying the weight. The verse says heaven declares the glory of the risen Lord and asks who can compare with his beauty. The chorus names him as the Lamb on the throne forever, and the singer bows and worships him alone. A later section says the singer will proclaim the risen Lord, who was once slain to reconcile man to God. Addressed partly about Christ and partly to him; the voice is a singular 'I' of response (bowing, proclaiming, worshipping), while the statements about Christ are creedal. The atonement is stated briefly as reconciliation, not unfolded.

claims.claim: All heaven declares the glory of the risen Lord, whose beauty has no equal.
claims.subject: The glory and incomparability of the risen Christ

claims.claim: Christ is the Lamb on the throne, and will be so forever.
claims.subject: The enthroned Lamb

claims.claim: The risen Lord was slain in order to reconcile man to God.
claims.subject: The purpose of the cross

claims.claim: The singer bows to Christ and worships him alone.
claims.subject: Exclusive worship of Christ

strengths.title: The slain Lamb reconciles man to God
strengths.explanation: The song states the purpose of Christ's death: he was slain to reconcile man to God. It joins this to his resurrection and his throne, so the gospel is present in a few words.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Reconciliation to God through Christ's death on the cross.

strengths.title: The Lamb on the throne forever
strengths.explanation: The chorus holds the crucified and the reigning Christ together as one Lamb, and gives him an eternal throne. It is the picture of Revelation 5.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The Lamb who was slain receives worship from all creation.

strengths.title: Creation declares, the singer bows
strengths.explanation: The opening echoes the Psalm's witness of the heavens, and the response is to bow and worship Christ alone, which fits the Bible's call to give him the worship due to God.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The heavens declare the glory of God.

doctrinesAffirmed: The atoning death of Christ as the Lamb
Reconciliation of man to God through Christ
Christ alone as the object of worship
theological.assessment: Nothing to correct. A short, Christ-centred song that joins the resurrection, the slain Lamb's reconciling work and his eternal throne, and responds with worship of him alone. The atonement is stated in one line and not developed, and the first-person response is the singer's own resolve. The sources read describe the song's background but give no independent evaluation of its teaching.

strengths.title: A short confession of the Lamb's reign
strengths.explanation: Its brevity and one-idea shape make it easy to learn, and its subject suits Easter, Communion and any service lifting up the reigning Lamb.

communal.vocalRangeNote: The same database lists the key as Bb. No chart was read; check the top of the chorus with your own room.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The chorus returns several times to the same confession of the Lamb on the throne and the response of worship; the repetition dwells on a real statement about Christ rather than filling space.
communal.assessment: A short song with a single chorus and a plain shape that a congregation can learn quickly. The singular voice is a first-person response, which most congregations can sing together as one act of worship.

strengths.title: Christ is named as Lord and Lamb
strengths.explanation: The risen Lord and the Lamb on the throne are named plainly, and the cross is stated as reconciliation, so the praise has a clear object and a clear ground.

clarity.assessment: Clear. Its imagery is biblical, its subject is the risen, reigning Lamb, and its one statement about the cross is plain.

synthesis.summary: A short song in which heaven declares the glory of the risen Lord, who is the Lamb on the throne forever and was slain to reconcile man to God, with the singer bowing to worship him alone. The voice is a singular response; the atonement is stated once and not developed. No false claims found; the sources give background but no independent assessment of the content.

scriptureReferences.relevance: The heavens declare God's glory, as the song opens.
The Lamb who was slain is worthy, as in the chorus.
